en: The Great King of Tantras of the Supreme Yoga of Non-dual Equality,
Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

Translated by the Dharma-transmitting Master, the Purple-robed Subject Shi-hu, by Imperial Decree. Part One: The Section on Images. The Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality, Part One: The Section on Images. Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the palace of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, together with a multitude of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas numbering as many as the atoms in ninety-nine Mount Sumerus. Each of these Bodhisattvas was a member of the retinue of Vajrasattva; their names were as follows:

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samacittotpādadharmacakrapravartin, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganasambhava, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvamāranirghātan—these and other such great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas were the leaders.

At that time, through the majestic power and sustaining grace of all the Tathāgatas, that celestial palace was endowed with every kind of supreme adornment; it was draped with banners, streamers, parasols, exquisite rare jewels, hanging bells, and strings of pearls interlaced and suspended. Great maṇi-jewels emitted radiance, shining extensively in various colors, as pure and perfect as the orb of the moon.

The Buddha, the World-Honored One, constantly dwells in the samādhi of the vajra empowerment of all Tathāgatas and in right wisdom; he has received the vajra initiation of all Tathāgatas, wears a jeweled crown, and occupies the station of the Dharma King of the triple world. He has realized the sovereign mastery corresponding to the omniscience of all Tathāgatas, perfected the equal mudrās of all Tathāgatas, and accomplished the most supreme activities of all Tathāgatas. Abiding in the body, speech, and mind of the Great Compassionate Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, which eternally dwell in the equality of the three times as a vajra, he is able to fulfill all vows throughout the entire realm of sentient beings. He is praised by all Tathāgatas in common and receives the exhortations of all Tathāgatas to preach the Dharma.

Furthermore, as many Buddhas and Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River have come from the worlds of the ten directions to assemble in this gathering, like sesame seeds filling Jambudvīpa; each of these Tathāgatas also constantly teaches this secret dharma-gate of non-dual equality in their respective Buddha-fields.

At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Vajradhara, abiding in the hearts of all Tathāgatas, cultivating the practices of all Tathāgatas, following the conduct of the bodies of all Tathāgatas, and acting in accordance with the intentions of all Tathāgatas, thus encompassing the entire family correspondence and dwelling according to the fundamental method, remained within this assembly with his body concealed and invisible.
At that time, as all the Tathāgatas assembled from the ten directions could not see the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi within the assembly, they immediately spoke these verses with one voice:
“O Great One, Vajrapāṇi! Like our very own father and mother, You do not appear within this assembly; Where has the Mahāsattva gone now?”
After those Tathāgatas had spoken thus, each remained silent within their respective Great Vajra Jewel Empowerment Dharmas.
At that time, the Great Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi emerged from the five places of all the Tathāgatas and manifested the form of the Buddha Mahāvairocana through his own physical appearance.
Again, from the hearts of all Tathāgatas, there appeared a great moon maṇḍala, brilliantly illuminated by hundreds of thousands of kinds of circular lights.

Having thus appeared, there again appeared from the hearts of all Tathāgatas a great sun maṇḍala, as vast as countless hundreds of thousands of worlds; he then returned to his original form and sat serenely within it.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas who had assembled immediately each turned toward the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, joined their palms in prostration, and requested him to teach the Dharma, speaking these verses:
“Excellent, O Vajra, supreme Dharma! Excellent, O Vajra, pure eye!
Excellent, O Vajra, most excellent wisdom! You universally encompass the omniscience of all Buddhas.”
We entreat Vajrapāṇi to universally bring benefit and happiness to all Buddhas,
and to proclaim the supreme secret Dharma of the Mahāyāna, which arises from the wisdom of both self and others.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Vajradhara, addressed the Tathāgatas, saying:
"The Tathāgatas, the Buddhas, should not exhort me to proclaim this secret dharma-gate."
The Tathāgatas said:
"For what reason and by what causes do you not speak?
Vajrapāṇi replied:
“O Buddhas, you should know:

among this great assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas here now, there may be some who, upon hearing the exposition of such a supreme ultimate truth and secret dharma of the Mahāyāna, will manifest various signs of disruption and the like.”
The Tathāgatas said:
“We shall each empower this assembly with our supernatural powers and cause them all to become a great host of Vajras; you need only now perform the Buddha-work.”
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Vajradhara, looked up at the Buddhas with a joyful smile and praised them, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
He immediately entered the samādhi called "The Great Wheel of All Tathāgatas, Radiant Light Universally Illuminating the Hearts of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from this samādhi, he manifested four great sun maṇḍalas in the four directions:

in the east, the Great Sun Maṇḍala named Holding Infinite Colors; in the south, the Great Sun Maṇḍala named Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Vajra; in the west, the Great Sun Maṇḍala named Immeasurable Vajra; and in the north, the Great Sun Maṇḍala named Amoghasamaya Vajra.
Having thus manifested, he then proclaimed for the assembly of all Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattvas this secret dharma-gate, the Sovereign Great Ritual Manual of Supreme Non-dual Equality.

That which he proclaims is in perfect accord with the principle of all bodhisattvas; it causes all bodhisattvas to accomplish the supreme meritorious qualities and the activities of supernatural power of all Tathāgatas, so that they may dwell in accordance with the principle throughout the entire assembly and even to the ends of the ten directions among all Buddhas and bodhisattvas.

Just as the light of space universally illuminates the trichiliocosm, and all the light of the solar discs shines everywhere according to their respective measures, so too it is with the light of all Tathāgatas and the light of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva;
these lights blend and merge, shining forth in equality. One who contemplates this in accordance with reality abides in the true principle.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas immediately presented an ocean-like cloud of offerings born from the Samantabhadra of all Tathāgatas as an offering to the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Having made this offering, those Tathāgatas remained silent.

At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Vajradhara, entered the samādhi called "The Arising of the Supreme Secret of All Tathāgatas That Destroys All Darkness, Born from the Mind-Family of All Bodhisattvas’ Wisdom."
Emerging from this samādhi, he proclaimed the dharma-gate of the Wisdom Family (jñānakula) samādhi:
"Abiding in a mind of meditative concentration, one should contemplate a pure ocean of milk.
Within it is a great lotus flower, like crystal and the light of the moon."
Contemplating the seed-syllable of one’s own mind, which corresponds to one’s own dharma,
through this visualization, the maṇḍala of one’s own mind is accomplished.
This maṇḍala is one cubit in length and breadth.
In the four directions and the four intermediate corners, it is magnificently adorned with the four jewels.
Visualize its formation according to the ritual; fix the mind without distraction.
It is surrounded by radiance, blazing and shining everywhere.
Therein, according to the ritual procedure, one visualizes oneself as pure,
free from the conceptualization of a self and so forth, and immediately contemplates becoming the Buddha-body.
Having thus performed this visualization, the maṇḍala is accomplished.
Next, according to the ritual of the Wisdom Family (*jñānakula*), recite the Great Mantra (*mahāvidyā*) as follows:
"The mudrās employed for this Great Mantra are all in accordance with the ritual of the Wisdom Family;
by the power of this Great Mantra, one can extinguish all transgressions."
Visualize hundreds of thousands of stainless, supreme lights; furthermore,
according to the ritual of the Jñānakula, visualize the vidyārājas and others as subtle,
pure white light, and arrange them according to the dharma.
What is performed is explained based on this; otherwise, it is not visualization.
This is called "The Dharma Gate of the Vajra Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.
Abiding in the firmness of one’s own mind, the corresponding light-rays emerge.
Visualize the image of the Buddha and the form of Vajrapāṇi.
For those who seek siddhi, by following the Vajra-hand method and practicing in accordance with the Dharma, siddhi will not be difficult to attain.
If one relies on this dharma and visualizes according to the principle,
with one's own image remaining unmoving, one immediately becomes Vajrapāṇi.
All those who know the dharma and visualize in accordance with the dharma [attain the same].
Even as far as that space extends, there is no transgression or fault.
The marks of the Buddha and one’s own marks are of a single corresponding nature;
when the mind is concentrated in correspondence with them, all undertakings are accomplished.
From the marks of the Buddha-image, the wise one contemplates five places;
relying on the gateway of corresponding dharmas, they visualize Vajrasattva.
This is called the gateway of the Lord of all Tathāgatas.
Visualize the great mantra of one’s own mind, emitting the light of the Jvālāmukhī family,
in which a vajra appears, destroying all evils.
Whatever is performed by one’s own mind, visualize it as the accomplishment of bodhicitta.
Five lights appear, making offerings to all Buddhas.
This is further named "The Dharma Gate of the Lord of All Tathāgatas.
Contemplate the five maṇḍalas, surrounded by blazing light.
Visualize the universal image of the Buddha, achieving the Great Illumination (vidyā).
With a concentrated mind, contemplate one's own body, free from grasping at signs or conceptual discrimination.
Clearly visualize your own reflection as being equal to all Buddhas, without distinction.
The bodhicitta of one’s own mind arises through the union of visualization;
adorned by Vajrapāṇi, it gives rise to all ritual procedures.
If one abides in the contemplation of this union and contemplates Vajrapāṇi, [one attains the goal].
One should simply follow the ritual procedures and visualize the images of the Buddhas.
Desiring to contemplate the images of the Buddhas, one should carefully observe the syllables;
by contemplating the reality of the syllables, one immediately beholds the images of the Buddhas.
Yet within these words, one contemplates the reflection as being free from signs;
when contemplating in this manner, the visualization of meditative union is accomplished.
First, dwelling the mind on a single point, one visualizes the sun maṇḍala.
Contemplate one's own body as pure, situated within the maṇḍala.
Next, imagine that throughout the entirety of space, maṇḍalas appear everywhere.
By contemplating in accordance with the dharma in this way, one achieves the realization through visualization.
If one visualizes that solar maṇḍala in accordance with the practice,
one will achieve accomplishment by visualizing oneself as Vajrapāṇi;
if one accords with the ritual method regarding that Vajrapāṇi, [the same result follows].
One should visualize the images of all Buddhas until they are in accord with one's perception.
Furthermore, if one visualizes the solar maṇḍala in accordance with the visualization,
the four-seal maṇḍala will likewise be accomplished through visualization.
Whether the mind abides in a single place, or pervades the entire world,
even unto the limits of space, one does not transgress the Dharma.
Through the four seals of the maṇḍala, one immediately achieves meditative realization through visualization.
The solar maṇḍala is also accomplished through visualization;
if one is in union with the visualization of the solar maṇḍala,
then the images of all Buddhas are likewise accomplished through visualization.
By means of this method according to the Dharma, one visualizes the images of all Buddhas;
likewise, one should perform the visualization of the maṇḍala of the four mudrās.
If one accords with this, [one attains] the maṇḍala of the four mudrās.
One should thus visualize the images of those Buddhas.
This is called the Dharma-gate of the Dharma-King Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
Contemplating all ritual procedures, one should visualize them in conjunction with the lotus.
One should encompass the methods of visualization and so forth; otherwise, they will not be in accord with reality.
One should visualize oneself, dwelling firmly in a steadfast mind, arising from the bodhicitta, and manifesting the image of the Buddha.
This is the supreme secret, the teaching of Vajra-śānti;
the light of great benefit and wisdom shines forth with equanimity.
If one contemplates according to the ritual method, all aspirations can be fulfilled.
"Visualize Vajrasattva; this is called the Vajra Dharma.
"This is named the Gate of the Dharma for Universally Good Vajradhara.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra surveyed the assembly and immediately rained down oceans of clouds of offerings from all Bodhisattvas, filling the realm of empty space, as an offering to the Great Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi.
Having performed the offerings, they again prostrated with utmost sincerity and took refuge, abiding according to the Dharma.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas assembled there once more rained down oceans of clouds of offerings for all the Tathāgatas as an offering to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra within the assembly. Having made these offerings, from the vajra-bodhicitta there emerged the Perfect Radiance of the Aspect Illuminating All Tathāgatas, which shone forth everywhere.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra manifested a radiance of his own reflected image; this light was named "The Cause for Destroying Darkness through the Wisdom-Section of the Firm Application of All Tathāgatas. Within this light, he concealed his own physical form and manifested the form of Vairocana Buddha, and then spoke this Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the True Wisdom Section of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas:
"The knower of phenomena thoroughly understands All those things performed, The characteristics corresponding to meditative concentration, And the truly pure Dharma."
Visualize the sun maṇḍala, measuring one thousand *hasta* at its greatest extent;
within it is a moon-disc altar, in the center of which visualize the syllable *vaṃ*.
Around that syllable, further visualize the maṇḍalas of the four directions.
Measuring one foot in length and breadth, there are various colored lights,
and those flames pervade everywhere—
the four cardinal directions and the four intermediate corners. One should visualize the syllable Oṃ in each.
Each of those syllables appears, manifesting in various subtle and wondrous colors.
Next, one should follow the ritual procedure and, within the maṇḍala,
correctly and clearly visualize Vairocana Buddha.
And all the worthy deities within the maṇḍala; Within the solar maṇḍala,
one visualizes a lunar maṇḍala, and within that,
one visualizes oneself, from which the Great Joyous Dharma arises.
From the subtle mind, the maṇḍala of the pure moon appears;
the form of the great vidyā-syllables again appears within the mind.
Next, one should visualize the syllable Oṃ, with its pervasive, blazing radiance.
From within this radiance, all ritual procedures are produced.
One should then visualize the image of the Buddha and the forms of the various worthy sages;
that constitutes the visualization of the four-seal maṇḍala.
All one's own activities are the arising of all Buddha-dharmas.
Visualize the five-pronged vajra at the heart according to the ritual;
Visualize the four-seal maṇḍala and the great mantra at the forehead.
One should then visualize the form of a Buddha, surrounded by a halo of blazing light;
having passed beyond this world through that visualization, one enters again into another realm.
One should contemplate and visualize a sublime moon maṇḍala measuring one cubit.
Visualize yourself in the center, as Vajrasattva arises.
This is called the supreme samādhi dharma-gate of the Samantabhadra Wisdom Family.
One should visualize according to the ritual method the sun-disk maṇḍala.
Visualize yourself as pure, appearing within the maṇḍala.
Then, at its four corners, visualize Vairocana;
thereafter, visualize yourself again as becoming Vajrasattva.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva.
Furthermore, one should follow the ritual procedure to distinguish the sixteen deities,
performing the visualization in four groups, each abiding in its respective position."
All other worthy sages likewise visualize the Great Radiance of Mind.
This is called the Dharma-gate of Holding the Vajra.
Furthermore, one should, according to the ritual method, visualize oneself [as the deity].
There is a subtle syllable HŪṂ, which abides in the heart, rotating counter-clockwise;
manifesting the appearance of radiance, it is able to destroy all the evils of Māra.
This is further named "The Dharma Gate of the Lord of All Tathāgatas."
"Furthermore, one should visualize that within a single kṣaṇa, all the noble ones and sages are born,
manifesting images of light that shine forth universally and brilliantly.
All the marks of syllables are immeasurably vast and boundless."
Visualizing in accordance with the Dharma, one forms the image of Vajra.
Within this, all syllables give birth to the great mantra-words;
these innumerable mantras accomplish all dharmas.
From the forehead to the navel wheel, visualize the syllable of the Great Mantra;
when this visualization is accomplished, all visualizations are no different.
Chapter Two: The Section on the Samādhi of the Wisdom Family from the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality, the Wisdom Family Samādhi Section. Furthermore, the verse says:
"Next, visualize a great white lotus, as vast in measure as a chariot wheel and exquisitely pure;
within it is a sun-maṇḍala, which one should contemplate according to the ritual correspondence."
Again, one visualizes oneself appearing within it, born from Karma-vajra;
one immediately becomes the body of Karma-vajra, no different from Vajrasattva and the others.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Vajrasattva.
One should contemplate the pure great ocean of milk; visualize one's own body appearing within that ocean of milk.
Through the wisdom-observation that one's own body is itself the Buddha-body, the Buddha-body thus appears, filling the entire realm of space."
Furthermore, one contemplates the pure great ocean of milk, Which possesses various colors and wondrous radiance;
Within it appears the moon maṇḍala, And within that, one further visualizes the form of the sun disk.
Next, one contemplates one's own body as the Buddha-body;
through the corresponding generation of the various ritual methods, by imagining one's own body pervading all, it extends as far as the measure of all world-systems.
Again, one should visualize the great ocean appearing within the mind; within that ocean is a solar maṇḍala.
According to the ritual, one should meditate upon the forms of the Buddhas, surrounded on all sides by a wheel of radiant light.
Within that light, syllables appear, as vast in extent as all worlds;
one should visualize them according to the ritual application of the *Veniśa* and other [tantras], in accordance with the Dharma.
Furthermore, one should visualize according to the ritual:
within a moon maṇḍala measuring one cubit, a vajra-sword appears, capable of accomplishing the rites for worldly attainments.
Next, visualize a white lotus with blazing light, representing the adornment of the bodhicitta;
within it, visualize the forms of the sages and deities of one's own family, with the *utsargas* (emanations) arrayed to the left and right.
Thus, by receiving [the teachings] according to the Dharma, one accomplishes all Vajra Dharmas;
pervading all worlds in this manner, one thus makes offerings to all Buddhas.
"This is called the Secret Dharma Gate of Samantabhadra.
Furthermore, one should visualize a sun-disk maṇḍala, equal in size to a tala tree;
within it, one visualizes the syllables of the Great Illuminator (Mahāvijñāna) gradually becoming more subtle, until all corresponding [deities] arise."
Firmly and securely abiding in one's own reflected image, one should then visualize the noble deities and others;
having placed the seed-syllables of the heart-mantras upon each, one universally makes offerings to all Buddhas.
Next, visualize the maṇḍala of the four mudrās, each measuring seven tāla trees in extent;
within the maṇḍala, visualize the various sages and deities, each with the seed-syllable of their heart-mantra arranged in its proper place.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Vajra Samādhi.
Next, one should visualize the maṇḍala, measuring one krośa in extent;
within it, one should imagine oneself as the body of a Buddha, together with that Buddha-eye Bodhisattva and others."
All things arise from the mind’s own conceptions; Through the observation of great wisdom, they are accomplished.
When that mind attains such correspondence, One achieves the corresponding contemplation of a Great Being.
Furthermore, one should visualize the maṇḍala of one’s own mind, its extent equal to one krośa;
observing that one’s own reflected image is unarisen, it does not transcend even the limits of space.
Abiding firmly in the gateway of self-correspondence, one corresponds by visualizing the Buddha;
abiding firmly in the gateway of Buddha-correspondence, one corresponds by visualizing Buddha after Buddha.
Visualize the bodhicitta in union with the visualization, its magnitude vast and pervasive throughout all things;
from this, all worthy sages are born. According to the ritual, visualize the syllables of the great mantra.
Visualize the sublime lotus in union with the visualization, its extent as broad as a *tāla* tree;
with the mind abiding peacefully and unmoving within itself, imagine it formed into the maṇḍala of one’s own heart.
Again, one should visualize the maṇḍala of one’s own mind, one tāla tree in extent;
one should visualize one’s own reflection appearing within it, whereby all that is performed becomes virtuous and firm.
Furthermore, one should visualize the white and pure light of Jvālāmukha, visualizing it five or six times in succession;
one should imagine one's own reflection situated within it, with the *yūṣmad* and *asmad* pronouns arranged to the left and right.
The vast radiance manifests according to the Dharma; from one's own mind arise white and the other seven colors.
Thus the radiance pervades all of space, within which one visualizes the forms of all Buddhas appearing.
Visualize one's own image pervading all of space; everything manifests from one's own mind.
One's own body and the Buddha-body are fundamentally in accord; all marks and characteristics function according to the Dharma.
Next, one should visualize all the bodhisattvas, filling the entire expanse of space;
their individual characteristics are in accord with reality, and all buddhas and bodhisattvas visualize them together.
According to the ritual, summon all the worthy sages and holy ones;
Abiding within the maṇḍala of space, their mutual characteristics correspond to the principle of ultimate reality; This is the visualization of the bodhicitta.
The great brilliance of the syllables and their correspondences— Contemplate those characteristics of the syllables as they truly are:
Born from the bodhicitta, They are adorned with blazing radiance.

From the light, various ritual methods appear; the self-image and the Buddhas are equal, with the images of self and others in perfect correspondence, radiating with the brilliance of a flaming garland.
Next, visualize that the Buddhalocanā Bodhisattvā and other noble beings appear according to the ritual;
with their respective heart-mantra syllables, they are arrayed within the moon maṇḍala.
The true form of Vajrasattva enters entirely into the midst of the subtle, wondrous light.
"This is called the Vajradhara Dharma-gate.
Furthermore, one should visualize the arising of Vajrasattva within the maṇḍala that is the reflection of one's own mind;
this sign corresponds to meditative observation according to principle. To observe otherwise is not the way to achieve accomplishment."
Furthermore, one should visualize the birth of Vajrasattva, appearing within a solar maṇḍala;
with various marks such as the vajra-hook and vajra-noose, he gathers the disciples and causes them to enter the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, one should contemplate the arising of Vajrasattva: all phenomena manifest from one's own mind;
they are provisionally designated by means of letters and so forth, and for this reason they fall within the category of letters.

Whether reciting mantras or performing ritual acts, if one abides in each instance with a mind fixed in meditative concentration, then through such practice, success will be attained; such a vidyādhara is called supreme.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas:
'Arising from one's own reflected image, one should contemplate clearly within the dharma of one's own family;
by contemplating that one's own mind abides according to the rite, all māras and adversaries are shattered and dispersed.'"

In this regard, one should thus seek siddhi; following the ritual procedures for various visualizations and so forth, in accordance with the maṇḍala of the solar disc, one should visualize the forms of the various vidyārājas.
One should visualize all the light manifested within the Yamāntaka family as having a wrathful appearance.
The characteristics he has explained according to the ritual procedures are called words of definitive truth;
one should contemplate them in this way according to reason, for to contemplate otherwise will not lead to accomplishment.
"This is called the Universal Samantabhadra Dharma-gate of all Tathāgatas:
'Visualize one's own reflected image as the maṇḍala, within which is a blazing and magnificent radiance;
its light shines universally throughout all worlds, all of which manifest from the mind of true wisdom.'"
One’s own body further appears within a lotus flower, illuminated by pure radiance;
though this body currently manifests as a form-body, its self-nature is equal and free from attachment.
Contemplate the syllable *citta* according to the ritual method; this is the form of Vajrasattva.
Since the form of Vajrasattva is universal, it is the contemplation of the forms of all Buddhas.
Knowing that the Great Mantra teachings give rise to them, one shall obtain all *siddhi* dharmas;
therefore, the Great Mantra is most supreme and honored—apart from the Great Mantra teachings, there is nothing higher.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Firm and Valiant of All Tathāgatas.
One should visualize the maṇḍala of the solar disc, with Vairocana Buddha appearing in its center;
one should contemplate that Buddha’s heart-mantra, for that mantra accomplishes all dharmas."
From this great illumination, there further arises The rare and supreme secret rite;
Everything manifests from the mind according to principle, Like the moon, pure and radiating light.
Furthermore, visualize that from one's own reflected image arise the signs of accomplishment, such as the vajra-sword and others;
these are produced according to the ritual procedure.
Visualize them appearing as a vast mass of light, possessing various colors and being exceedingly subtle, universally illuminating the world in its infinite extent.
"This is called the Dharma Gate of the Samādhi-Eye of All Tathāgatas.
Thus ends the first fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-advayasamatā-parama-yoga-mahātantrarāja-sūtra*.
The Buddha-spoken *Advayasamatā-parama-yoga-mahātantrarāja-sūtra*.
Sūtra Scroll II.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Purple-Robed Subject, under Imperial Edict.

Part Three: The Section on Samādhi of the *Tattvasaṃgraha* Division. The Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality. At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the *Candramaṇḍala* (Moon Maṇḍala) of all Tathāgatas; he then manifested the form of the Buddha Mahāvairocana through his own body and dwelt within the great maṇḍala of the *dharmadhātu*.
Having thus established oneself, one returns once more to the self-characteristics and explains the *samādhi* dharma-gate of the *Tattvasaṃgraha* section:
"One should visualize a pure great ocean of milk, adorned with the four supreme jewels;
within that ocean, an *utpala* lotus appears. With a mind of focused concentration, one should contemplate the syllables of the Great Mantra."
In accordance with the Maṇḍala of the Wisdom Family, this visualization method is most supreme.
Arising from the wrathful form, one should skillfully contemplate the corresponding radiance;
that very radiance pervades all, and one should visualize the form of Vajrasattva.
In accordance with the Dharma, one further contemplates one’s own reflection, abiding likewise within the radiance.
This is called the Vajra Dharma Gate of the Samādhi of Gathering the Families.
The Great Vidyā of this Family is:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgata-saṃgrahājñāna-svabhāvātmake svāhā. This King of Vidyās is born from the King of the Family’s Ritual Manual; one should perform visualization according to the ritual manual of this Family.
In this context, "one's own image" refers to the form of the syllable *HŪṂ*; all visualizations should be performed in reliance upon this.

All such ritual procedures (*vidhi*) arise from this syllable *HŪṂ*, which is subtle and inconceivable. Within a single instant, it gives birth to all the noble deities (*ārya*), and from one's own image and so forth, equal radiance manifests; thus, the seed-syllable of one's own mind becomes the maṇḍala.

"When that mind correctly contemplates, it is in accord with all dharmas; those characteristics of syllables are the characteristics of the wisdom of dharmas. Therefore, one should contemplate through contemplation in accordance with reality; this is called the Vajra Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas."
“If one applies oneself to the five locations according to the ritual, one should visualize a five-pronged vajra arising from those syllables of the great mantra.
Visualize the form of Vajrasattva; according to the ritual, a great radiance appears, shining universally throughout the buddha-fields.”
"This is the Dharma-gate of the Supreme Son of Vajrapāṇi.
Through union with Vajrapāṇi in his own form, one should visualize the insignia of Vajrapāṇi;
know that the images of all Buddhas will arise, their vast radiance illuminating the world."
“This is called the Dharma-gate of the Wisdom of One’s Own Reflection:
‘In union with the Vajrapāṇi of one’s own mind, adorned by the blazing garland of flames,
born from the bodhicitta, its vast radiance illuminates the world.’”
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Self-characteristic Benefit.
Visualize this buddha-field appearing as light, with flaming garlands shining everywhere;
from the visualization of its own characteristic, [arise] the vajra-hook, and arrange it according to its own reflected image."
"By means of the ritual, summon all Tathāgatas; They all enter into the light.
This is called 'The Dharma-gate of the Lord of All Tathāgatas.
In union with the assembly of one's own reflected images, Visualize those syllables of the great mantra."
Great radiance appears according to the ritual method; visualize the form of Vajrasattva.
The bodhicitta arises as its own reflection; with a concentrated mind, visualize the true principle.
Through union with the visualization of this true principle, all māras and adversaries are shattered and dispersed.
If all manner of māras and adversaries arise, performing acts of wrath and terror,
one should contemplate that they are born from the bodhicitta, manifesting transformations throughout the world.
Visualize one’s own form appearing within the solar disc, adorned with vast and great rays of light;
from this, the various ritual procedures arise—the sublime purity of Karma-vajra.
All phenomena originally arise from correspondence; With a firm mind, they dwell securely in goodness.
The ritual of all phenomena is proclaimed according to principle; Primordially corresponding, they are naturally equal.
A sign appears within the utpala lotus, Pervaded by various colored lights;
In harmony with the signs of all the worthy and holy ones— Thus one should perform the supreme visualization.
The great mantra-syllables pervade the three realms, Extending even to the maṇḍala of space;
All arise from the images of the Buddhas, White in color, luminous, and wondrously pure.
Within the pure and wondrous moon maṇḍala, one should visualize according to the ritual;
corresponding to the form of Maitreya, one should always contemplate thus according to the dharma.
One should likewise imagine the image on the cloth:
Vajrasattva radiates light, his own reflected image blazing intensely, adorned with the forms of Māmakī and the others.
Furthermore, one should visualize the arising of Vajrasattva and his manifold transformations throughout the vast worlds;
each is manifested by firm, steadfast wisdom, and one should contemplate them in union with the wrathful deities.
Great radiance appears according to the Dharma, merging with the radiance of its own reflected image;
therefore, within the solar maṇḍala, one perceives the self-characteristic of wisdom without obstruction.
Visualize the great five-pronged vajra, vast as the world, manifesting transformations;
born from the image of wrath, it is adorned with the seed-syllables of its own family.
Contemplate the form of the Great Wheel according to the Dharma;
within that wheel, visualize the Buddha’s body, with corresponding light radiating everywhere—this is called the visualization of correspondence.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Vajra Self-nature.
Furthermore, within the wheel, one should visualize oneself, adorned with a precious sword and manifesting radiant marks;
the bodhicitta is itself a garland of light, appearing everywhere as the signs of supernormal power."
Next, one should visualize a wondrous lotus flower in the mind, adorned with the blazing radiance of Brahma;
born from the bodhicitta, the syllables of the great vidyā-mantra are extensively arrayed upon it.
The mind appears as the visualization of an *utpala* flower, possessing various colors and wondrous radiance;
abiding in the bodhicitta according to the method, one visualizes the syllable of the great mantra within meditative concentration.

Furthermore, one should visualize that from within one's own heart there appears a subtle, great light of sapphire-blue, born of the union with great wisdom; therein, one should contemplate the image of the Buddha.
Furthermore, one should visualize that within one's own reflected image, there appear various subtle and blazing lights;
within the mind, one visualizes the form of syllables, and within those syllables, one contemplates the image.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Firm Wisdom.
Furthermore, one should visualize a most supreme and subtle maṇḍala measuring one cubit in size;
within it, one should visualize the syllable of one's own image, pervaded by vajra-flame light."
Furthermore, one should visualize a maṇḍala of supreme great wisdom measuring one cubit;
within it, imagine the emergence of one's own image, and while in meditative concentration, recite the vidyā-mantra.
Furthermore, one should visualize a pure solar maṇḍala measuring one cubit in size;
within it, one visualizes the emergence of Vajrapāṇi, while in meditative concentration reciting the vidyā-mantra.
Furthermore, one should visualize a space measuring one cubit, wherein the Karma Maṇḍala is accomplished;
therein, one visualizes the subduing of all māras and enemies, while reciting the mahāvidyā-mantra within meditative concentration.
Furthermore, visualize a Tāla tree in height; within it is the supreme Maṇḍala of Great Wisdom.
Contemplate your own image therein, and you will immediately become the Buddha Vairocana.
Furthermore, one should visualize a lotus maṇḍala, equal in size to a single tala tree;
within it, one should visualize one’s own image appearing, while observing the forms of all Buddhas to the left and right.
Furthermore, one should visualize a subtle maṇḍala, equal in measure to one krośa;
within it, one should visualize one's own reflection appearing, manifesting transformations throughout the entire world.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Vajramahāsattva.
Furthermore, one should visualize a pure moon-maṇḍala, equal in extent to one krośa;
within it, one should visualize the image of the Buddha appearing, with the two *yūthī* flowers arranged to his left and right."
One should visualize that *uṣṇīṣa* as constantly manifesting five kinds of wondrous light;
within those lights appear pleasing flowers, various clouds of subtle fragrances,
and other such supreme articles of offering— visualize these offerings being presented to all the Tathāgatas.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Vajra Eye.
According to the ritual, one should visualize the *ūṣṇīṣa*, its form yellow and exquisitely adorned, arranged all around the Buddha’s seat;
one should imagine it arising from the union of the *saṃyoga*."
Just as they arise and act, one should visualize the form of Vajrasattva;
because Vajrasattva has arisen, one should visualize him according to the ritual of his respective family.
Furthermore, one should visualize a great, subtle maṇḍala of wisdom measuring one krośa;
with self and others' reflections perfectly corresponding, contemplate it clearly as appearing therein.
Relying upon the supreme Vajra-dharma within oneself, one should contemplate the five colors as the five aspects:
white should be known as the Mahājñāna family; black represents the Tattvasaṃgraha family;
red is named the Padma family; and yellow is named the Kāma family.
The supreme excellence of leftward-turning wondrous colors, the manifestation of adornment among all adornments,
the wondrously blooming great lotus— this is the very activity performed by the Vajra.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Great Secret Lord Vajra.
'Such a secret method of correspondence should not be revealed to those who do not correspond.
If one abides in the firm gate of its own characteristic, even other dharmas will be accomplished.'"
For one who performs this corresponding visualization, imagine the appearance of the body of Uṣṇīṣavijayā, with exquisite color and the most supreme of all ornaments;
upon seeing her, you should feel love and joy, and not give rise to fear.
Furthermore, one should visualize the form of Vajrasattva, filling this buddha-field and manifesting everywhere;
as the firm reality that is the reflection of all Buddhas, the Great Vajra Dharma universally encompasses all.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Destruction by the Three Vajras. Chapter Four:

The Section on the Samādhi of the Dharma Family from the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality, the Section on the Samādhi of the Dharma Family. At that time, the Great Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi again taught the Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the Dharma Family:
"All that is to be performed is explained based on this; The great maṇḍala is thus brought into correspondence."
In this regard, according to the ritual procedure, one should visualize the accomplishment of the Dharma Family (Dharmakula).
One should abandon the conceptualization of grasping at signs; instead, one abides in the sign of the correspondence with all phenomena.
Regarding the gateway of visualizing all correspondences, the great mantra of the Dharma Family is recited as follows:
"This clarifies that through visualization and recitation in accordance with the Dharma, one immediately accords with the Great Samaya.
Arising from all natures, herein there is neither nature nor absence of nature."
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara.
One should visualize a pure and wondrous lotus; this flower symbolizes the purity of desire.
Purity itself constitutes the maṇḍala, appearing within the visualization of one’s own pure characteristics."
Furthermore, one should visualize the Great Illuminating King being born as a vast and blazing mass of light;
that radiant glow completely pervades everywhere, and within the light, one visualizes the manifestation of Avalokiteśvara.
"This is further called the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara:
'Visualize one's own form appearing within a moon disc, with various colored rays of light pervading everywhere;
those rays illuminate everything, even filling the entire realm of space.'"
Next, one should visualize the form of the most excellent vidyā within one's own heart;
by visualizing oneself as identical with that, one is adorned by the wisdom of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, visualize within the dharma-maṇḍala the appearance of the most supreme Vidyārāja,
who is born from Avalokiteśvara and manifests transformations throughout the world-systems.
Furthermore, within the Dharma Maṇḍala, one should contemplate Avalokiteśvara with a concentrated mind;
born from Vajrasattva, he manifests transformations throughout the world.
"This is called the Gate of Samantabhadra.
Furthermore, within the Dharma Maṇḍala, one should visualize the manifestation of the most supreme Avalokiteśvara, the true birth of Vajrasattva;
one should contemplate according to the ritual through the correspondence of the five places."
"This is further called the Dharma-gate of Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, within the mind one should contemplate the subtle and supreme Great Dharma Maṇḍala, which arises from the pure lotus;
all manner of emanations appear therein according to what is appropriate."
Furthermore, within the mind, one should contemplate the subtle and stainless great dharma maṇḍala;
therein appears a pure lotus of wondrous color, and within that flower, one should clearly visualize the forms of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, one should clearly visualize within one's own mind the supreme Great Dharma Maṇḍala;
therein, one visualizes the manifestation of Avalokiteśvara, which is the visualization of the forms of the five Buddhas.
Furthermore, one should clearly visualize at the navel center the supreme Great Dharma Maṇḍala;
within it, one visualizes the manifestation of Avalokiteśvara, which is itself the visualization of the forms of the five Buddhas.
Within the Dharma-maṇḍala, one should visualize a single tārā tree according to its own characteristics;
one should visualize that it arises from its own characteristics.
Within the maṇḍala, all ritual procedures and the various rites that arise therefrom extensively perform all acts of offering.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Holding the Lotus.
Furthermore, one should visualize the Great Dharma Maṇḍala, measuring one krośa in extent;
within it, one should clearly contemplate oneself as being the very form and appearance of Avalokiteśvara."
Furthermore, one should visualize a lotus maṇḍala, equal in extent to one krośa,
with *yojana*s appearing to the left and right; performing acts of worship with various mudrās,
in accordance with the maṇḍala of one’s own mind, one should then contemplate the dharma-maṇḍala.
Throughout all world-systems, one extensively manifests the ritual procedures for making offerings;
through union with the maṇḍala of one’s own mind, one should then visualize the Great Wheel Maṇḍala.
Relying on the ritual manual of the Sun Maṇḍala, one should visualize one’s own reflection entering into its center;
visualizing the syllable of the Great Mantra upon the crown of the head, it extends even beyond the limits of space.
Visualize five kinds of wondrous lotuses, with the stainless radiance of the lotuses manifesting;
one should understand this according to the ritual method and visualize one’s own image in the center;
visualize the image of the Buddha in the east, and visualize it as being born from that.
In the south are the *Caryā* and other sections, whose activities are equal and harmonious;
in the west are the practices of the Supreme Dharma;
and in the north, the *Kāma* section arises.
The vajra-wheel is used in the Jñāna family; the vajra-sword is used within the Dharma family;
the vajra-pestle performs the rites of the Saṃbhoga family; and the trident is common to the rituals of those three families.
One should know that they pervade the entire realm of space;
according to the rites performed by each of those families, all arise from the noble sword, the vajra, and the supreme dharmas.
The light of the flame of desire is extremely blazing, extending extensively throughout the entire dharmadhātu;
arising from the vajra trident, it does not destroy its own reflection.
Corresponding with the maṇḍala of one’s own mind, one should know that this revolves within the Wisdom Family;
corresponding with the maṇḍala of Great Wisdom, one should know that this revolves within the Gathering Family;
corresponding with the maṇḍala of the Sublime Dharma, one should know that this revolves within the Dharma Family.
Corresponding to the Maṇḍala of the Sublime Moon, one revolves within the Kāma family;
corresponding to the Maṇḍala of the Solar Disk, one should revolve within all families.
"This is further named the Dharma-gate of Holding the Lotus. Chapter Five:

The Section on the Samādhi of the Kāma Family, from the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality, the Section on the Samādhi of the Kāma Family. At that time, the Great Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi placed the great vajra of all Tathāgatas within the various secret families, such as the Jñāna family, and entered the maṇḍala of the correspondence with that Great Wisdom to establish the activities to be performed. Within that great maṇḍala, he established his own image and the images of all Buddhas, bodhisattvas, and holy sages.
Having thus entered into accordance with the Dharma, he then spoke the samādhi dharma-gate of the Kāma family:
"All that is to be performed is explained based on this; The great maṇḍala is attained through such correspondence.
One who contemplates according to the Dharma achieves accomplishment; To view otherwise is not true contemplation."
Regarding all the ritual procedures of the Kāma family, the vidyā-mantra of that family is proclaimed as follows:
“Such are these subtle and wondrous vidyā-words, Which accord with the equality of phenomena;
Born from the great lotus, Pure radiance pervades them entirely.”
Relying on this dharma, visualize the maṇḍala; within it, further visualize your own image.
From this, the image of Kāma-jvālā arises, manifesting transformations vast as the world.
Corresponding to the self-characteristics of the kāma-dharmas, reaching even beyond the limits of space,
it arises as the reflected image of the Brahmā King, universally adorned with various blazing rays of light.
From the kāmayana arises the reflected image, manifesting transformations throughout the world;
in this manner, according to each ritual procedure, one should visualize three kinds of images.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of Kamāgni.
Furthermore, one should visualize a sublime lotus, one cubit in length and breadth;
within that lotus, one should imagine radiance, in which the image of Brahmā appears."
Furthermore, one should visualize a great lotus, measuring one hundred and eight cubits at its highest point, arising from the reflection of Kāmajvālā;
therein, one visualizes the forms and marks of the three Buddhas.
Furthermore, one should visualize a great lotus, measuring one hundred and eight cubits at its highest point;
from it arises the image of Nārāyaṇa, and within that flower, one visualizes the Buddhas and others.
Know that from the image of the Buddha arises the transformative activity of the image of Brahmā;
from the image of the Dharma is born the appearance of the image of Nārāyaṇa;
the firm function of the appearance of Vajrapāṇi, and the appearance of Kāma-jvāla, are born from this.
In accordance with the dharmas appropriate to what should be done, they appear pervading the entire world.
Furthermore, one should visualize the image of the Great Brahmā King; that image is vast, measuring a thousand cubits.
From the heart of this Brahmā King, the images of all Buddhas appear within the visualization.
The images of all Buddhas appear according to the Dharma; the form of Nārāyaṇa is likewise.
This is further called the Dharma-gate of Kāmārcis-prabhā.
Again, one visualizes the arising of Kāmārcis-prabhā, with the form of Nārāyaṇa measuring one thousand cubits.
Arising from within this mind, the images of all Buddhas appear within the sphere of perception.
All these images of the Buddhas are entirely in accord with the *kāmayāna* dharma;
according to the ritual procedures for their arising, they are most excellent, adorned by the *līlā*.
"Even until the dharma corresponding to the image is attained, that *yojana* is immediately accomplished.
This is called the supreme *kāmayana-prabhā-dharmaparyāya*."

Chapter Six: The Section on the Accomplishment of All Supreme Wisdom through Samādhi, from the Supreme King of Great Ritual Manuals of Non-dual Equality, titled "The Section on the Accomplishment of All Supreme Wisdom through Samādhi. At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Vajradhara, again proclaimed this dharma-gate:
"For those who seek siddhi, Within the rites of their own family (*kula*), In accordance with the maṇḍala, One’s own image arises."
According to the ritual manual of one's own family, one should visualize the Sun Deity;
abiding in *samādhi*, one achieves accomplishment through union.
With great wisdom, one contemplates the image as pervading the entire realm of space.
Visualizing the various forms and signs, one abides in samāhita.
Those signs of the various devas should be understood according to the Dharma;
this is indeed a marvelous teaching, which no evils can destroy.
Such is the method of the Great Seal; this is explained according to the principle of reality.
The four kinds of great mantra-words are to be performed in accordance with the ritual system.
All those actions are in union with samādhi.
All visualizations are inseparable from the gateway of samāhita;
the minds thus aroused are for the universal benefit of sentient beings.
Through the visualization of their own characteristics, the inner mind becomes vast.
If one conceives doubts regarding the dharma of samādhi,
the Buddha says that such persons possess an inferior spiritual lineage;
if one understands this dharma, they should possess great merit.
Thus one should know according to the Dharma; otherwise, it is not visualization.
Just as the utpala lotus and others are born from within the mud, so too should all of them be known as the stainless characteristics of the mind itself.
The bodhicitta is firm and is sustained by all Buddhas;
it arises from Vajrapāṇi, and is not produced otherwise.
The great elements, such as earth and the rest, arise according to their respective supports.
This purity is likewise so; it is the supreme dharma of the Wisdom Family.
This is called the "Dharmaparyāya of Samantabhadra.

Chapter Seven: The Section on the Profoundly Secret Offering of All Buddhas, from the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality. At that time, the Great Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi remained empowered within the form of the firm and wondrous moon maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Great Wisdom Born from All Vajra-Samādhis," and within that very samādhi, he further entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Wisdom of All Corresponding Samādhis."
Emerging from this samādhi, he taught the Dharma-gate of the Birth and Non-birth of Wisdom for the Secret Accomplishment Corresponding to All Samādhis:
"The birth of the Buddha’s image, The various colors and radiant lights,
The correspondence with the maṇḍala, And the methods for accomplishing the wheels and so forth."
Abiding in samādhi, one should visualize the measure of a *cāṇakya* pervading the entire maṇḍala.
Placing the syllable of the great vidyā upon the forehead, one should practice according to the rite for one month.
Visualize and seek accomplishment;
when you see flowers filling the sky, these flowers are most exquisite and wondrous.
Visualize them as forming a maṇḍala; these flowers are the insignia.
This signifies the mark of accomplishment.
Like the measure of a small grain of wheat, adorned with the light of a flaming garland—
this is the arising of the corresponding [state].
Visualize a five-pronged vajra appearing at the tip of the nose, corresponding with the color of sapphire and the like;
visualizing such a form and appearance, one should visualize the formation of a maṇḍala, such as that of the utpala lotus.
All are the ritual procedures of the Wisdom Family; arising from within the phenomena of the Dharmadhātu,
they are visualized, manifesting vast radiance that pervades the realm of empty space.
Its flower has eight petals, the size of a jujube fruit, with pure light pervading everywhere.
Do not give rise to divergent thoughts; it is free from the divisions of beginning, middle, and end.
Visualize with equanimity;
imagine it appearing throughout the ten directions. According to the ritual of the Kāma family, visualize the manifestation of pure radiance.
In the measure of a small grain of wheat, adorned with the radiance of flames,
it manifests the characteristic of the Kāma family.
According to the various offerings appropriate to each— such as generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and so forth—
The meaning of firmness is likewise so.
All are equally empowered; the great luminosity of one’s own mind shines universally like the moon.
The vajra is equal, and all other directions and quarters are not to be visualized as being created;
that which is described as equality is the dharma of the Wisdom Family.
Through the union of those three families, Vajrapāṇi Guhyakādhipati is born;
abiding in the meditative concentration produced from that, one performs the activities without violating the *karmapatha* (ritual action).
Regarding the description of the adornments of the various marks:
the *utpala* lotus is used for the Wisdom Family (*jñānakula*) and the Gathering Family (*saṃgrahakula*);
the *padma* lotus is used for the Desire Family (*kāmakula*) and the Dharma Family (*dharmakula*).
Ten, twelve, and sixteen are used respectively in the Jñāna, Saṃbhoga, and Dharma families; twenty,
according to the ritual procedure, is used within the Kāma family.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Secret Samaya of All Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, according to the secret method, one performs acts such as adornment;
born from the Buddha, one makes equal offerings."
Adorned with sandalwood incense, one immediately accomplishes the *karmavajra* rite;
yet if doubt arises in the mind, it destroys the *maṇḍala* rite.
When all things are equal, doubt does not arise.
"If doubt arises, the Buddha says it is not accomplished.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Heart of All Tathāgatas.
"The practitioner, according to the rite, bathes and adorns themselves."
Within all the aspects of the signs, there is neither destruction nor deficiency.
If one relies upon this samādhi, one will achieve realization;
if one transcends the gateway of this samādhi, one shall not achieve realization.
This secret dharma-gate is the most supreme reality;
if one penetrates it without obstruction, accomplishment will be achieved free from doubt or fear.
One should draw a four-cubit maṇḍala according to the ritual injunctions.
Relying on the great mantra of one’s own family, recite it five hundred thousand times;
seek accomplishment according to the ritual method, for otherwise it will not be achieved.
This is called "The Dharma Gate of the Radiance of All Tathāgatas."
"From Vajrasattva, who is born of reality,
one should draw the supreme maṇḍala, measuring one cubit in length and breadth.
[It is the domain of] the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja, Amṛtakuṇḍalī."
Relying on the equality of the Dharma, one bestows the supreme accomplishment.
Within the maṇḍala, according to the ritual procedures, one installs the vajra-hook and other implements;
by making offerings of incense and flowers, one shall immediately attain accomplishment.
Furthermore, by the shore of the great ocean, or in a secluded place among the mountains,
one should paint the maṇḍala of one's own family according to the rite and to the best of one's ability.
With various precious offerings, one should make offerings to Vajrapāṇi.
And having visualized the Honored One Avalokiteśvara, one should perform the rite with a concentrated mind.
During the two periods of the night— namely, the first watch and the middle watch—
the practitioner enters the maṇḍala to seek the siddhi of reality.
Thus, after half a month, one attains correspondence with what is to be practiced;
even for those who have committed the most grievous sins, success is achieved by seeking this Dharma.
This Dharma is the gate of equality, free from the conceptualization of grasping at signs.
Through the empowerment of Vajrapāṇi, all shall attain supreme accomplishment.
Born from the Lord of Secrets, they attain equality with all worlds and achieve incalculable *koṭis* of accomplishments.
Manifesting the bodies of all Buddhas, equal in measure to Mount Sumeru,
born from Vajrapāṇi, he brings benefit to sentient beings.
