Chapter Eight: The Supreme Secret Section on the Wisdom-Realization of All Tathāgatas, from the Sovereign Great Ritual Manual of Non-dual Equality, the Supreme [Tantra] of All Tathāgatas’ Wisdom-Realization. At that time, all the Tathāgatas who had come from the ten directions again exhorted Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!...”

I pray that you will proclaim the samādhi of the realization of wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the samādhi of great mantras, and the samādhi of the lion-like transformations for the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas—the Dharma gate of the equality of great wisdom for swiftly realizing *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, having heard these words from all the Tathāgatas, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, first placed the vajra upon his own heart and performed an empowerment; he then spoke these words:
"The Buddhas should not repeatedly exhort me to proclaim the dharma-gates of the various samādhis."
Why is this? Because this Dharma is profoundly deep, supreme, and secret; it is the dharma-gate for the accomplishment of the True Wisdom Seal (*jñāna-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas.
Should those of inferior faculties hear this Dharma, there will arise a thousand kinds of signs of destruction and the like.
The Tathāgatas said:
"We, all the Buddhas, collectively empower you; you should now proclaim [the teachings] as appropriate.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, abiding within the supreme and wondrous Moon Maṇḍala at the heart-peak of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed the Dharma-gates of the Great Mantra Samādhi and the Samādhi of the Wisdom-Realization of All Tathāgatas:
"All the incalculable Buddhas do not break the gateway of the union with reality;
the practitioner attains the Buddha-body in the present life, and all that they do is definitively certain.
All the Buddhas, numbering in the tens of millions, do not break the union with the wisdom of the Buddhas."
The practitioner attains siddhi in this very life, And achieves the body of Vajrasattva.
Gathering all multitudes of sentient beings Into a single vast lotus-sized expanse,
Through samādhis and all such dharma-gates, They are able to attain siddhi in every respect.
Encompassing all methods for attaining *siddhi*, Equal in measure to a vast and great lotus, The wise should contemplate this with true reality:
It arises entirely from the light of *kāma-jvāla*.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Innate Purity.
'Visualizing [the deities] pervading the realm of space, with all Buddhas universally manifesting various bodies—
without breaking such a true reality, the practitioner shall attain siddhi in this very life.'"
Contemplate the true reality of your own mind; all actions will then be pure.
This is the samādhi that is unbroken and originally unborn; anything other than this is not the practice of correspondence.
Myself and all classes of sentient beings—our minds are fundamentally pure and luminous;
though possessing various natures, they are entirely unstained. Contemplate with clarity that the mind is equal to the gateway of reality.

All the supreme activities of all Buddhas, Each and every one practiced according to the Dharma in its true reality, Give rise to the pure and luminous Great Enlightenment; To practice otherwise is not accomplishment.
Therefore, the Great Illumination is most supreme and victorious; it can accomplish the most sublime secret dharma.
Born from the purity of Vajrasattva, to practice otherwise is not the Great Joy.
The meaning of mastery over those supreme activities is that all that is done and all that is practiced is entirely equal;
the wise know this according to reality, while those who differ from this are called the foolish.

The practitioner should know things as they truly are: whether walking, standing, or even drinking and eating, by not violating the samādhi-gates of all Buddhas, one shall swiftly attain the *siddhi* dharmas.
All clouds of incense and flower offerings, Produced in accordance with all that is meaningful,
Arising from the nine *mudrā* gates, Are offered to all the worthy ones and sages.
By constantly maintaining the secret vidyā of one’s own family, one immediately attains the dharma of Vajrasattva;
this is the samādhi-gate of the realization of true wisdom, belonging to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas.

'The practitioner, dwelling well in a firm mind, / According to the ritual procedures of that maṇḍala, / Performs all activities as they are normally used; / Everything should be done accordingly, free from doubt.'"
All that is to be done should be performed according to this method; what is done otherwise is not in accordance with it.
The self-accomplishing rite is most vast, as taught by the Wisdom Vajra;
whether for oneself or for others, all ritual applications—even those arising as far as the limits of space—should be practiced thus.
If one does not accord with ultimate truth, one will not achieve success in the Buddha-dharma.
Worldly suffering, pleasure, greed, hatred, and delusion are all equal because they are free from the mark of self.
By realizing that the nature of greed, hatred, and delusion is empty, one is naturally purified without abandoning greed and the rest.

Chapter Nine: The Section on the All-Secret Samādhi of Vajrasattva; The Supreme Great Ritual Manual of Non-dual Equality. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāguhyapati Vajrapāṇi again proclaimed the Dharma-gate of the All-Secret Samādhi of Vajrasattva, which is the cause of the Great Wisdom of all Tathāgatas:
“Those who practice the supreme yoga should not pay homage to the śrāvakas;
they should instead pay homage to those Tathāgatas, and thus attain the accomplishment of the corresponding dharma.”
The practitioner should, regarding their own reflected image, meditate according to the ritual method on the true principle;
all acts of worship performed within the wheel of one’s own mind and so forth are thus brought into correspondence.
If, among all those sentient beings, there should be anyone who transgresses this secret,
their head shall immediately split into seven pieces, and they shall further fall away from the bodhicitta.
If one abides in the secret gateway, reciting the secret vidyā-mantra employed for practice,
one should clearly visualize oneself as the image of Vajrasattva, who has arisen therefrom.
The Buddha is the supreme ācārya; he who is most excellent among all, ever providing skillful protection, and who has realized the secret reality—this ācārya is no different from the Buddha.
Visualize all the Buddhas and Ācāryas as arising from the bodhicitta;
through meditative union with one's own reflected image, all true activities are fully accomplished.
All mantra-holders should understand that [the goal] arises from the samādhi of reality;
through such correspondence with this samādhi, one transcends it, whereas those who deviate from the samādhi do not achieve accomplishment.
Furthermore, one should visualize one's own form arising from the secret of Vajrapāṇi;
through the correspondence with the accomplishment of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) and so forth, one should practice the preliminary rites as desired.
Whether by time or by application according to the ritual rules, this samādhi is the most supreme;
when one constantly practices in accordance with it, one will eventually attain all siddhis.
One should practice the preliminary dharmas as desired, whether in terms of time or application;
this samādhi is supreme, and one should always guard it well in all circumstances.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of the Great Bodhicitta.
'Born from one's own reflected image, Abiding in a single aspect within that very image, One’s own mental measure is vast and boundless;
Thus one practices the preliminary rites of the Great Illuminator.'"

One should know that this samādhi of great wisdom, in which all actions are free from faults, focuses single-mindedly on performing the rites of protection; thus, the siddhis sought will be well-established.
Contemplate all Tathāgatas according to the Dharma-truths; with a concentrated mind, contemplate the signs of *siddhi*.
From the birth-gate of Vajrasattva, the accomplishment of the Dharma corresponding to one’s own mind arises.
The practitioner should always rely on this ritual procedure, performing visualization during the three periods of the day;
if one recites the mantra otherwise than according to this method, that which they perform will not be a *siddhi*.
The image and the image are without distinction; blazing with the fierce ornaments and radiant light, one should visualize them as arising from the Jewel-Hand, the supreme and vast Vajra-Jewel.
Perform the visualization according to the equality of the Dharma, until the signs of siddhi are perceived;
if one acts otherwise, one is deluded and shall not achieve accomplishment in the secret [teachings].
The supreme crown of great wisdom and wondrous jewels, Exquisitely adorned and perfectly pure—
Apart from this gateway to the supreme siddhi, There is no other dharma that is more excellent.
Abiding securely in the great wheel of Vajrapāṇi, Untainted by attachment within the three realms of existence, I have accomplished the wisdom-vajra;
I constantly proclaim the pure syllables of dharma-wisdom.
The dharmas of Amṛtakuṇḍalī and others abide through that empowerment;
as space is immeasurable and boundless, I emerge from the virtuous dharma.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Vajradhara.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahā-Guhyapati Vajrapāṇi further spoke this Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas, which is the Great Wisdom, Great Purity, and True Purification of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas through the empowerment of the Vajra:
"Furthermore, this is explained as the Mind-Vajra; Visualize the arising of Vajrasattva."
Having visualized the mind in this manner, one is immediately able to enter that Wisdom Vajra.
Regarding the meaning of the self-nature purity of the Vajra, one should skillfully observe the Vajra of Speech;
visualize the gateway of the pure Great Wisdom, for Great Wisdom turns according to that vocal activity.
The vajra body is firm and indestructible; The sublime light shines through vajra empowerment.
That very svabhāvakāya of all Buddhas Abides thus, empowered according to the Dharma.

By relying on such dharmas, one attains bodhi; Abiding through empowerment within the Vajradhātu, If one practices according to the dharma for six months, One will immediately obtain the siddhi-dharmas of all Buddhas.
The dharma of desire is unborn and unstained; all things arise from that vajra.
By practicing according to this true ritual procedure, all siddhis will be fully perfected.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, further spoke the Samaya of the Great Wisdom Ācārya of all Tathāgatas:
"One should know that the three kinds of wisdom arise equally; all improper speech is not in accordance with reality.
By practicing according to principle based on the ritual of the True Dharma, one attains the accomplishment of a Buddha-Ācārya."
One should visualize those Buddhas and their equals, completely filling the expanse of space;
visualizing them as arising from the Great Illumination, one should take delight in the mind of samāhita.
All those who delight in the Dharma should constantly visualize the Buddha-ācārya within the subtle and supreme maṇḍala,
and with a focused mind, recite the great vidyā-mantra of their own family.
The images fill the entire realm of space; Visualize within the mind the manifestation of the Buddha’s body.
This is what is called practicing according to the principle; Abiding in the true wisdom of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, one should visualize the Maṇḍala of the Sublime Moon, appearing from the aspect of the reflected image;
according to the ritual, recite the vidyā-mantra of one's own family and perform the visualization while coordinating it with the five points of the body.
Abiding in the thought of awakening according to the ritual, with all branches perfected and fully delighted,
enter that Dharma-maṇḍala and maintain the recitation of the great vidyā-mantra of one’s own heart.
Visualizing all supreme and wondrous jeweled crowns as the act of vast offering,
one makes offerings through true union with the Buddha-ācārya, the gateway of great bliss.
By reciting the mantra of the tutelary deity according to the ritual, one remains far removed from all fears;
if this method is applied with realization for even a moment, one shall attain Buddhahood in this very life.
"This is called the Dharma-gate of Equal Benefit in All Places.

The Tenth Chapter: The Section on the Samādhi-Siddhi-Maṇḍala of All Samādhis, from the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality. At that time, all the Tathāgatas who had come from the ten directions again emerged from the adornments of the body, speech, mind, and wisdom of all the Tathāgatas, and produced clouds of offerings to worship the Bodhisattva Mahāguhyapati Vajrapāṇi. Having thus made these offerings, they all spoke these words:
"O Mahāsattva!..."
"Please explain the supreme maṇḍala of the reality of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), which accomplishes the wisdom of all samādhis.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having received the exhortation of all the Tathāgatas, immediately entered the samādhi of the vajra empowerment of the equality of all the Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from this samādhi, he proclaimed the supreme great maṇḍala of the reality of meditative concentration,
which accomplishes the wisdom of all samādhis: "Now I shall explain the accomplishment of the wisdom of samaya,
The supreme and vast maṇḍala, Produced by the great vajra-wisdom, The awakening of all Buddhas, as it truly is."

With a concentrated mind, visualize within the ocean of milk the appearance of a pure and sublime lotus, adorned everywhere with various necklaces; focus your attention and maintain this visualization.

The maṇḍala measures sixteen cubits; abiding according to the rite of the Buddha-ācārya, its form is square with four corners, and the four gates are to be visualized and arranged according to the rules.
Visualize a maṇḍala of a lunar disc within; furthermore, a Jambu tree appears.
According to the ritual, visualize five-pronged vajras arrayed at its four outer corners, and visualize those five-pronged vajras performing empowerment in five locations.
Furthermore, within that moon disc, one should visualize the positions of the Buddhas according to the ritual:
in the east, as prescribed by the rite of their respective families, install Akṣobhya Tathāgata and the others;
in the south, likewise according to the rite of their respective families, install Ratnasambhava Tathāgata and the others.
The Buddha Amitāyus and others of the west, Amoghasiddhi and others of the north—
According to the colors and forms of each direction, Abide in the reality of the mind and perform the visualization;
In the center is Vairocana Buddha, Visualize him as the source from which all ritual procedures arise.
The various ritual applications within the maṇḍala should be visualized according to the sequence of the teachings.
Furthermore, one should visualize the Bodhisattva Locanā and others at the four corners within it,
as well as the Vidyārāja Amṛtakuṇḍalī and the other vidyārājas at the four gates.
Thus, regarding the physical forms and other characteristics of the noble ones, one should visualize each according to the ritual procedures;
visualizing them completely in their respective directions and sequences, all in accordance with the method of Vajrasattva.
One should know that from the five radiances emerge the five dharmas, complete and as one desires;
these are the Buddha-ācārya samādhi-gates, and all that is performed relies upon the dharma of samādhi.
Furthermore, one should visualize that the realm of empty space is entirely filled with all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones;
universally making offerings to them through the secret dharma, one should contemplate and recite according to the secret teachings.

Chapter Eleven: The Great Samādhi Section of the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality, the Great Samādhi Section. At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, further expounded the great samādhi maṇḍala of the *Amoghasamaya*:
"All that is to be performed is taught based on this, The gate of great wisdom of the Buddha-ācārya.
In accordance with the solar maṇḍala, One should visualize everything according to the ritual method."
In the east, the supreme of all phenomena, visualize the rite of Vajrasattva;
In the south, the ultimate and victorious vidyā-mantra, visualize the rite of Vajrasattva;
In the west, the wisdom of the supreme perfect enlightenment, visualize the rite of the Buddha-ācārya.
In the northern directions, one should visualize the various *saṃtrāsas* according to the method of Vajrasattva;
in the center, within the vast and equal three realms, one should visualize the image of the Great Vajra.
Having visualized the color white throughout all directions, one should again visualize the color black in the center;
one contemplates the wondrous marks of the *yuṣmanta*, performing deeds according to the Vajra Dharma.
Maheśvara-Vajrasattva, visualize all forms and appearances;
according to the ritual procedures, visualize the Buddha’s image with a mind of focused concentration, golden in color as appropriate.
In this manner, according to the ritual procedures, one should visualize the form of the Wrathful Vidyārāja, the mantra of one's own family, and the five dharmas;
universally, one should perform offerings with the vidyā-mantra.
Extending even to fill the entirety of space, one visualizes the form of Vajrasattva;
having made offerings with the various great mantras, one further performs the secret dharma offering.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi called the Vajra Empowerment Born of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from this samādhi, he further taught the maṇḍala of the Tathāgata Subhavyūha:
"In accordance with the maṇḍala of the Sublime Dharma, one should visualize everything according to the ritual method;
abiding in a mind corresponding to meditative concentration, one should clearly contemplate that all phenomena are without self."
In the east is Holder of the Radiance of the Sublime Dharma; in the south, Great Wisdom, Vastness of Dharma;
in the west, Sublime Dharma, Great Sovereignty; in the north, Arising of the Sound of the Supreme Dharma;
and in the center, Sovereign Lord of the Sublime Dharma— one should visualize them according to the ritual procedure as appropriate.
Having visualized the color white throughout all directions, one should further visualize the color red in the center.
Within the ritual of this particular family, being sovereign over the Dharma, one should contemplate with a focused mind the four corners,
[visualizing] the wrathful Vidyārāja Hayagrīva and others, and according to the rite, install them at the four gates.
The five dharmas are fully endowed with all perceptions; they accord with the method of secret offerings.
In the center of the mind, one visualizes the manifestation of a wondrous lotus, and around its perimeter, one further visualizes the dharma of sublime bliss.
Manifesting precious jewels filling the realm of space, One contemplates the secret gateways of one’s own dharmas;
Through the threefold correspondence of secret offerings, The Dharma-ācārya acts according to the ritual manual.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi called "The Firm Empowerment Born of the Vajra of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas."
Emerging from this samādhi, he further taught the Great Samādhi Maṇḍala of the Purification of All Defiled Phenomena:
"In accordance with the Kāma-maṇḍala, one should visualize everything according to the ritual rules:
in the east is the great radiance of Śakra; visualize various pure and wondrous colors."
In the south is the Great Sovereign of Blooming Flowers; contemplate his self-nature as being without nature.
In the west is the Great Dharma Wisdom Purified; contemplate with focused mind the mark of tranquility.
In the north is the Most Victorious and Supreme; visualize purity according to the ritual procedure.
In the center, one should perform the union with Kāma and, according to the ritual, visualize one's own image.
According to the rite of the Kāmeśvara family, one should clearly visualize the selflessness of mind;
then, all the supreme Lotus-Hand deities should be visualized and placed in the four corners according to the ritual.
Visualize those five factors as being fully complete, and perform offerings as is appropriate.
Born from Vajrasattva, visualize them surrounding [the deity] according to the ritual procedure;
through union with the secret *kāma* dharma, the most supreme offerings are produced.
The activities of the Kāma-ācārya, the acceptance of secret offerings and so forth, are the constant duties of the Buddha-ācārya; he is the venerable noble one of that maṇḍala.
Having visualized the Vajrācārya, that supreme maṇḍala of all,
according to the meaning of the Karmācārya, there is no further need to explain the maṇḍala separately.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the vajra-samādhi called the empowerment of the crown of the hearts of all Tathāgatas, which illuminates them all.
Emerging from this samādhi, he proclaimed the Great Dhyāna Maṇḍala of the Heart-Crown of Vajrasattva, which illuminates all:
"Visualize with a concentrated mind a great ocean of milk; Within it is a pure, great lotus flower.
In the center of the flower is a mountain of crystal jewels, Adorned in various ways, most exquisite and wondrous."
Upon the mountain peak, visualize the Dharma-maṇḍala according to the ritual;
contemplate it with a mind of focused attention, complete with its four sides, four corners, and four gates, each endowed with its respective features as prescribed by the rite.
The Great Illuminating Queen is born from the center; visualize her wheel-mark according to the ritual.
One should visualize the East with a mind of truth, following the rite of Vairocana Buddha;
one should visualize the South with a firm mind, following the rite of that Amitāyus Buddha.
In the west, one should likewise visualize the Buddha-Usnīsa King of Light-Mass according to the ritual;
in the north, one should contemplate it with correct reasoning, for such is the supreme method of its arising.
Visualize that which arises from the reflection of the Dharma, with exquisite colors and forms surpassing those of the *uśīra* flower;
visualize that the accomplishment of his excellent gift is entirely of one vajra-nature.
Visualize all the Buddhalocanā Bodhisattvas and others, arranged according to the ritual procedure in the four intermediate directions;
visualize the invincible wrathful Vidyārāja (Aparājita) positioned at each of the four gates.
Visualize the venerable Vajrasattva; all that is in union with him is accomplished.
When the five dharmas are entirely complete, this is the offering of the union of wisdom.
Arising from one's own secret dharma, the generated offerings and so forth are non-different;
thus pervading the entire realm of space, visualize the appearance of the Sarvavajroṣṇīṣa.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi called "The Arising of the Vajra Empowerment of Universal Homage to the Equality of All Desire Realms."
Having emerged from this samādhi, he taught the Great Samādhi Maṇḍala of the Universal Lineage’s Equal Lion Transformation:
"First, one should visualize a vast, pure ocean of milk; Next, it further manifests in various colors.
Within these many colors is a great mountain, Adorned with the four jewels, most subtle and wondrous."
Upon the mountain peak, one further visualizes the maṇḍala: its four sides, four corners, and four gates, surrounded by blue utpala flowers;
one contemplates it as pure and magnificently adorned.
Within the maṇḍala, one should visualize a moon disc; within that disc, there are further seats of various jewels.
The Buddha-ācārya occupies the center of these, entering the gateway of the meditative concentration of union.
Within that solar maṇḍala, one should visualize with a mind of focused truth the birth of the vidyārājñīs,
the noble ones, and so forth, each arranged at the four corners according to the ritual method.
Those such as Amṛtakuṇḍalī, the wrathful vidyārājas of blazing radiance,
adorned with wrathful attributes, should be visualized as arranged all around according to the ritual method.
The consort of the lunar-maṇḍala, born from the union of the five places,
adorned with the vajra-ghaṇṭā, shines with the blazing light of the Jvālāmukhī family.
The Lord of Lotus Wondrous Bliss is pure, with a garland of blazing white light;
most supremely pure and exceedingly subtle, visualize him as being filled with the adornment of a jeweled crown.
Born from Vajrasattva, the Buddha-ācārya of most excellent marks,
adorned with various wonderful jewels— contemplate him according to the Dharma with a mind of truth.
Born from Vajrasattva, it is a great radiance of a garland of many jewel-flames;
within that light, an utpala lotus appears—this one should visualize in the eastern direction according to the rite.
Without giving rise to divergent thoughts, one should practice visualization: born from the Vajradharma, it emerges.
One should, according to the ritual, visualize in the south the Lotus Flower of Equal Radiance;
born from the Kāma-vajra, it is a wonderful parasol of red light,
its surrounding flames serving as a majestic adornment— one should, according to the ritual, visualize this in the west.
The vast golden light of wisdom should be visualized according to the ritual in the northern direction.
One should likewise visualize the sovereign mistress of the family vidyā in the four corners as appropriate;
one should contemplate the secret marks of what is to be performed, adorned with various exquisite jewels.
Delighting in and finding joy in the dharmas that correspond [to them], one should visualize and give rise to bliss as appropriate.
That Ācārya who is invincible should, according to the ritual, visualize the four gates;
like performing the secret vajra-stride, he should visualize exiting the triple world through these gates.
All appearances of reflected images should be visualized as the arising of Vajrasattva;
this is the constant practice of the Buddha-ācārya. Endowed with the five dharmas, all are pure;
performing the service according to the rite at all times, this dharma gives rise to great joy.
Furthermore, one should imagine that from one's own secret [nature] there arises the constant performance of supreme acts of offering;
visualizing these images filling the entire realm of space, one should perform offerings as appropriate.
All the great jewels of the kalpa-trees, as well as those pure wish-fulfilling gems—[one should offer them].
Distinguishing according to the various classes of dharma, one should visualize their respective forms and marks;
as each image is described, one receives empowerment in accordance with the ritual method.
If one follows the ritual procedures regarding those signs, one should visualize the supreme auspicious vase;
with the mental image of the Buddha’s form and so forth being identical in aspect, one should perform all offerings with a mind of focused contemplation.
If a practitioner performs the rite according to the principle, they abide in the state of correspondence;
such a person shall attain Buddhahood in this very life—this teaching is definitive and free from doubt.
This Great Vidyā-mantra of the Wrathful King of this Family skillfully bestows the methods of accomplishment as appropriate;
the practitioner shall, in a single instant, attain the perfection of the supreme siddhi.
The secret practices of all samādhi-gates, the Dharma-nature gate of the Buddha-ācārya—
what is taught is the truth and is further unified in mind, arising according to the characteristics of such a family.
The Buddha-Spoken Mahāyoga King of Tantras of Non-Dual Equality, Scroll Three.
The Buddha-Spoken Mahāyoga King of Tantras of Non-Dual Equality,
Scroll Four.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma (Shi Hu), Imperially Conferred Title of Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, wearing the Purple Robe, under Imperial Decree.

Chapter Twelve: The Emergence of the Great Samādhi. The Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality. Chapter Twelve: The Emergence of the Great Samādhi. At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi called "The Illumination of the Wisdom-Light of All Space Realms."
Having emerged from this samādhi, he proclaimed the vidyā-mantra of the Wisdom Family, the Dharma-gate for the manifestation of the Great Being of the Great Samaya, saying:
"Oṃ jyeṣṭhanupavāya svāhā. Once this vidyā-mantra had been spoken, hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya Buddha-fields all shook violently.
Furthermore, whoever hears this great vidyā-mantra shall immediately attain vast mnemonic power, eloquence, and wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi of the vajra empowerment known as the Samantaprabhāsa-samādhi.
Having emerged from this samādhi, he proclaimed the vidyā-mantra of the Gathering Family:

"Oṃ saṅkara-hayānubhava-vaya svāhā. Once this vidyā-mantra had been spoken, throughout the entire realm of space, a vast and blazing radiance spontaneously appeared, illuminating everything everywhere; it shone through one another with perfect transparency, perceiving all without obstruction.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi of intrinsic purity (*prakṛtiviśuddha*).
Emerging from this samādhi, he proclaimed the vidyā-mantra of the Dharma family:
"Oṃ dharmajñānodbhava svāhā. Having spoken this vidyā-mantra, a vast radiance spontaneously appeared, illuminating all boundless buddha-fields.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi called "The Adamantine Empowerment Born from the Auspicious Assembly of Innate Purity."
Emerging from this samādhi, he proclaimed the great vidyā-mantra of the Kāma family:
"Oṃ kāmanīyanudbhavaya svāhā. Having spoken this vidyā-mantra, a vast radiance spontaneously appeared, illuminating all infinite buddha-fields.

All vidyādharas, within their respective families, should understand it thus: they should give rise to the mind of union, abide in the principle of reality, remain empowered by their own reflected image, and contemplate with a mind of truth all that is to be performed.

"Furthermore, it should be known that the various mudrās of the various families differ according to their respective characteristics. That is to say: the joining of two arms and the joining of the fingers is the general mudrā characteristic common to all families; the joining of vajra-forms is the mudrā characteristic of the Wisdom Family (Jñānakula); forming the bind of jewel-forms is the mudrā characteristic of the Gathering Family (Saṃbhāra-kula); the arising of lotus-forms is the mudrā characteristic of the Dharma Family (Dharmakula); the Karma Family is no different from the Dharma Family; and forming the bind of trident-forms is the mudrā characteristic of the Kāma Family. This is called the Dharma-gate of the Great Mantra Bodhicitta."

13. The Thirteenth Chapter on the Initial Activity of the Supreme Great Vidya-mantra Teaching: The Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality. At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the samādhi called "The Vajra Empowerment Born from the Samādhi that Fulfills All Aspirations."
Emerging from this samādhi, he proclaimed the maṇḍala for the accomplishment of the Great Samaya:
"This maṇḍala is most supreme and vast; like space, it is expansive and immeasurable. This great accomplishment is no different from it."
If one wishes to paint this maṇḍala, one should act according to the ritual procedures of the respective family (kula) in accordance with the Dharma.

First, one should spread out the cloth for painting; then, having empowered five-colored threads according to the rite, one should measure the boundary lines. One should distribute the boundary lines in sequence so that they are perfectly aligned, and paint accordingly according to the prescribed dimensions.

That maṇḍala is constructed in three tiers, fully adorned with four sides, four corners, four gates, and four pavilions; each of the four gates is embellished with *nirghāta* ornaments, and paintings depict the appearance of precious jewels raining down from the sky.

Having thus laid out the threefold divisions of the maṇḍala, one should next paint the forms of the deities according to the ritual rules: in the center of the first inner circle, paint the Honored One of the Family; in the east, the Honored One of the Wisdom Family; in the south, the Honored One of the Gathering Family; in the west, the Honored One of the Dharma Family; and in the north, the Honored One of the Kāma Family. Having thus painted the four cardinal directions, all four corners should be painted in sequence according to the standard method.

"Furthermore, on the second outer layer: in the east, paint the Bodhisattva Mahāsitātapatrā (Great White Parasol) of the Most Victorious Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa; in the south, paint the Bodhisattva Vajradhara; in the west, paint the Bodhisattva Padmadhara; and in the north, paint the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī. In its four corners, one should paint the Bodhisattvas Locanā, Māmakī, Pāṇḍaravāsini, and so forth. These various bodhisattvas should each form the mudrā of their respective family and be painted according to the original ritual manual."

"Furthermore, on the third outer layer: in the east, one should paint Śakra, Lord of the Devas, together with the hosts of devas of the desire realm and the hosts of Śuddhāvāsa devas; in the southeast corner, the great ṛṣis possessing the five supernatural powers and the hosts of Agni; in the south, Bali, Lord of the Pretas, and the hosts of the seven mothers; in the southwest corner, Bali, Lord of the Pretas, and the hosts of bhūtas; in the west, Varuṇa, Lord of the Waters, and the hosts of nāgas; in the northwest corner, Vāyu, Lord of the Winds, and the hosts of vidyādharas; in the north, Kubera, Lord of Great Wealth, and the hosts of yakṣas; and in the northeast corner, the Lord of Bhūtas and the hosts of bhūtas. These various deities and others should each be painted according to their respective rites."
"Furthermore, at each of the four gates, paint a Vajrasaṃhāra Bodhisattva; and in the four corners outside the third tier of the maṇḍala, paint five-pronged vajra scepters."

"Once the deities have been thus arranged and depicted, one should, according to the ritual procedure, place the auspicious vase (*bhadraghaṭa*) along with incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments to perform offerings and present secret offerings. One should empower them according to the dharma to request the joy of the honored deities, and according to the dharma, one should place the implements for secret offering at its four gates."
Having performed this secret offering, one shall, by relying on the instructions of the Great Mantra (vidyā), immediately obtain the gracious joy bestowed by the Honored One (iṣṭadevatā).

That vidyādhara should first perform the rite of generating the offering for Pīṭhacaṇḍālī, next for Hārītī, and finally for the entire host of bhūtas; having done so, he should further perform the homa ritual using the vidyā-mantra of his own specific family (kula).

"This maṇḍala is most supreme, excellent, and wondrous; as it is a word of truth, it can bring about accomplishment, and even the conferral of initiation upon disciples and various ritual activities will all be achieved. This is the method for union with Vajrasattva, the most supreme functional gateway of all Buddhas."

The Buddha-ācārya has expounded this gate of samādhi according to the principle; all Buddhas throughout the paths of the three times are able to perform the great empowerment (*abhiṣeka*), even unto its emergence from space. Just as it emerges without obstruction like a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*), so too is my true arising—the basis for all empowerment methods—unobstructed in the same way.
"If a person hears the name of Vajrasattva or beholds his form, they shall attain the supreme stage within seven lifetimes.

If one wishes to abide in the ocean of wisdom empowered by the Buddha-ācārya, that vidyādhara should constantly make offerings to the Buddhas, the Great Munis; thus, they will be taken under the care of the Buddha-ācārya as a disciple of his family."

As previously explained regarding the five kinds of samādhi, one should practice visualization with single-minded concentration according to reality; thus, one becomes an adept who achieves accomplishment within the Great Samaya Maṇḍala, which is called the "True Arising of the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel."

At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, having established himself in the empowerment of the hearts of all Tathāgatas, and desiring to cause all practitioners of yoga to abide in the activities of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, entreated the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, to proclaim the dharma-gate of the supreme accomplishment.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, spoke this Dharma-gate of the primary practice for the supreme accomplishment of the samaya of all Tathāgatas:
"Now I shall explain the vast maṇḍala, With a measurement of thirty yojanas;
Its form is square with blazing light, And it is completely pervaded by the great light of indranīla."
Space is unimpeded and pervades all; visualize it in conjunction with meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
Furthermore, visualize the dimensions of this Jambudvīpa continent as being entirely filled by a vast, pure ocean of milk.
Within that ocean, a great lotus flower appears, its size equal to that of a chariot wheel.
Within the lotus, one should visualize Yamāntaka, the wrathful vidyārāja with a laughing countenance;
according to the ritual, one should visualize his form, with physical features and insignia as prescribed by the standard rules.
Or manifesting a frowning, wrathful countenance, with the blazing light of the Yamāntaka family intensely radiant—
whatever arises according to the ritual procedure, one should visualize it as non-different from those [deities].
The Great Vidyārāja Nīlananda is visualized with the wrathful form that destroys the three realms;
he is encompassed by all Buddha-dharmas and abides in the true wisdom of all Buddhas.
The three kinds of images, as described, should be visualized as pervading the realm of space;
their forms arise according to the dharma, while one’s own mind is visualized as being free from all characteristics.
One’s own mind and all those reflected images should be clearly visualized as the forms of the noble ones;
furthermore, by gradually condensing the great luminous syllables, one should visualize the noble ones residing therein.
According to the ritual procedures for the great radiance of the kalpa-fire, one should dwell with a mind in meditative concentration and perform universal visualization.
Visualize that the pure and blazing moonlight is one's own body, which, according to the constant dharma,
is born from the noble ones and sages.
One's own mind manifests its own reflection; Visualize according to the method without distinction.
All the great mantra syllables herein Are perfectly capable of fulfilling all aspirations.

Thus is the first dhyāna described; the practitioner should contemplate with single-minded focus, visualizing the blazing great light of the kalpa-ending fire, wherein the Lord of the Family, the Principal Deity, constantly appears.
One should dwell in meditative concentration and clearly contemplate all the characteristics of the vidyā-mantras;
visualizing them in perfect correspondence with the images of all Buddhas within the maṇḍala of the wondrous moon.
Again, visualize that from one's own heart there arise emanated Buddhas from every pore of the body,
filling the entire realm of empty space; one should contemplate the three great vidyās appearing in conjunction with five-colored light,
and install the deity according to the ritual procedure.
In accordance with the ritual methods of the Great Illuminating King, arrange everything according to the principle of reality.
Visualize all Buddhas within the realm of space, their manifested bodies filling it entirely without any vacancy.
Having first visualized the primary deity and the noble sages, one should then visualize them all as being completely pervasive.

Chapter 14: The Section on Accomplishing Activities from the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again proclaimed the Dharma-gate of the teaching on the differentiation of all secret great vidyās:

"Furthermore, one should visualize within the sky the manifestation of a maṇḍala of the four directions, vast in measure for incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) yojanas, most supreme, expansive, and all-pervading."
One should abide in meditative concentration with a mind that accords with reality, visualizing one's own reflection appearing therein as Vairocana Buddha,
abiding in accordance with reality through the correspondence of the five places.
Next, visualize the maṇḍala of the solar disc, and imagine all the noble deities appearing within it.
Vajrasattva manifests from one’s own heart; visualize him as arising according to the ritual method.
Furthermore, one should visualize the solar disc of pure light, blazing and filling the entire realm of space;
all the signs of the various sages and saints are in perfect correspondence, which one should visualize as being arranged according to the sequence of the ritual.
The wise should know that this class of teachings is the truly pure doctrine;
anything other than this is not a gateway to accomplishment and is far removed from the practice of secret meditative concentration.

Chapter Fifteen: The Emergence of All Great Vidyās and Vajras from the Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, Part One of the Supreme Great Ritual King of Non-dual Equality. At that time, the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata again taught the method of dhāraṇī-recitation for the true teachings of all Tathāgatas:
“Space is boundless and has no directions; Know that one’s own mind is likewise so.
Having visualized the external maṇḍala, One should contemplate the self-maṇḍala as non-different from it.”
Wherever the flower falls, that is the deity; visualize the true method of union.
Having visualized the Mahāmudrā according to principle, one should not visualize any other phenomena.
Within one's own mind, visualize the subtle, pure maṇḍala of great wisdom;
from it, one's own reflection appears as white light, signifying its establishment from the aspect of great compassion.
All the syllables and phrases of the great vidyās, one should visualize according to the initial secret dharma;
the insignia of the five-pronged vajra—those too should be visualized in this manner according to the rite.
The dharmas arise from one’s own reflected image; the wise one is well-established in five locations.
The various syllables follow the gates of their characteristics, as they are conceived arising from meditative concentration.
The words and phrases follow the ritual manuals; one should visualize them as a rosary for the sake of mindfulness.
According to the specific applications of the various families (kula), the wise should understand them as they truly are.
Visualize that which is born from great wisdom; by reciting it with single-minded devotion, it is perfected.
It is upheld by all the Buddhas, and it skillfully proclaims the perfect Dharma.
The true dharma of the single-syllable vidyā-mantra: visualize it in union with its own reflection;
The true dharma of the three-syllable vidyā-mantra: imagine it as produced from the Lord of the Family;
The five-syllable vidyā-mantra and so forth are sustained, even unto the dharma of the arising of syllables.
Universally manifesting white, blazing light, its flaming garlands shine forth in all-pervading brilliance.
From the beginning, according to the Dharma, one discerns the various activities performed by the families:
with the appearance of blue *utpala* lotus petals, it universally manifests the great radiance of indranīla-blue.
Manifesting vast light according to one's own family, visualize that accomplishment with a concentrated mind.
The form of the Lord of Lotus Bliss is red in color, with blazing light pervading everywhere;
the light that appears according to the ritual procedure shines universally throughout the world.
Yellow and yellow light are extremely blazing, Everything appears everywhere as yellow.
Just as one should visualize the various forms and signs, They will certainly be accomplished;
Arising from their own reflections, They truly manifest exactly as described.
Visualize your own mind appearing as a wondrous flower, which then transforms into a maṇḍala;
therein, according to the ritual procedure, one should clearly visualize the true Great Seal (mahāmudrā).
One should contemplate the true great wisdom as it arises from the Verses on the True Dharma;
one should visualize it as arising from the root, performing offerings to all Buddhas and so forth,
manifesting various miraculous transformations according to the Dharma throughout all world-systems.
Furthermore, gradually condensing the visualization of the truths, Without beginning, middle, or end, all are as they truly are;

This corresponds to the radiance of the wondrous moon. One should visualize the method of the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) accordingly, And understand the rituals of the three families according to principle; This is the teaching of true purity.
All undertakings shall be brought into harmony; one should visualize according to the appropriate ritual procedures.
If the visualization of the specific rite has not yet been perfected, one should contemplate the supreme Dharma of sublime bliss.
The practitioner should enter a quiet dwelling, Abiding in the state of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) with its corresponding signs;
With single-minded focus, they should clearly visualize here The accomplishment of the body, speech, and mind of all Buddhas.
The practitioner who accomplishes this reality, focusing intently on the methods for attaining *siddhi*,
should clearly visualize the forms of the Buddhas and, adorned with a jeweled crown, perform offerings.
One should visualize the signs of the Buddha-ācārya’s manifestation within one's own mind;
clearly contemplating the supreme mudrā of the vidyā-mantra of one's own family, one should abide in meditative concentration upon the heart.
In accordance with the Dharma, the functions of eating, drinking, and so forth, all abide in the state of sovereign mastery;
even such matters as form and fragrance are entirely the vast and true mind.
The Buddha-ācārya is himself supremely blissful, always in accord with the Dharma of the noble ones;
herein, everything is performed according to the Dharma, for practice other than this does not lead to accomplishment.
All the great mantra syllables that have been taught can fulfill all aspirations;
these great mantras skillfully bring about all accomplishments, serving as the gateway to the wisdom of the true secret.
If one breaks the samādhi-gates of all Buddhas, both self and others are likewise destroyed;
know that all such conduct and actions are like improper speech.
All phenomena arise from all Buddhas; they are accomplished through the birth of Buddha-wisdom.
Born from the form of Vajrasattva, the dharma of Vajrasattva is accomplished.
If one attains correspondence with the four practices, universally encompassing the root of all noble sages,
and maintains the fundamental dharma according to the Dharma and according to principle, this is called a Vidyādhara.
These dharmas are all the Buddhas, the truly secret, virtuous, and immovable;
this is the essence of the supreme vidyā-mantra, which one should visualize with equanimity as appropriate.

Having correctly analyzed the various classes of dharmas and visualized the images of all Buddhas, one should visualize their wheel-marks as appropriate; all arise from the reality of one's own dharma.
The practitioner should constantly visualize the noble deities such as Vajrasattva;
according to the ritual procedures for the equality of the three families, they shall remain without decline or destruction until the end of their life.
Blessed by Vajrasattva, all the various methods of accomplishment of the Buddhas,
all the vidyās and gates of great joy— the accomplishment of samādhi is explained according to reality.
At that time, the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Tathāgata again entered the samādhi of the Vajra Equality of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from this samādhi, he proclaimed the Vajra Maṇḍala of the Birth of All Tathāgatas:
"All ritual actions are explained based on this; one should draw the Samaya Maṇḍala."
In the east, one should paint the Honored One Akṣobhya, manifesting his primary mudrā according to the ritual rules;
in the south, one should paint the Honored One Ratnasambhava, following all the rites of his own family;
in the west, one should paint the Honored One Amitāyus, likewise according to the methods of his own family as appropriate.
In the north, according to the ritual manual of one’s own family, one should paint the Honored One Amoghasiddhi;
in the center, in accordance with the authentic ritual procedures, one should paint the form of the Buddha-ācārya.
Next, draw a five-pronged vajra, adorned with garlands of flames and radiant light;
arrange it according to the ritual method to seek accomplishment, just as the Buddha-ācārya performed.
All actions depend upon the root mudrā; with the radiance of a blue utpala flower, one further draws an eleven-pronged great vajra, arranged according to the Vajra-dharma.
In the four corners of the inner maṇḍala, one should draw an utpala lotus in each;
know that these four great mudrās are no different from the marks of a universal monarch (cakravartin).
Furthermore, within the maṇḍala, one should draw the four jewels in four colors as ornaments;
accordingly, one should also depict the various hosts of devas and the worthy sages within the maṇḍala.
On each of the four gates, paint the various vidyārājas;
their colors and forms should all follow the rules of their respective families—namely white, black, red, and yellow—and each should be painted accordingly, one by one.
Having thus arrayed the forms of all the worthy sages, the practitioner should abide in a state of meditative concentration;
using respectively the root heart-mantras of each worthy sage, they shall skillfully accomplish all dharmas and destroy all evils.
At its four gates, according to the ritual procedures, one should constantly perform secret offerings;
even those consisting of food and drink, all are performed while abiding within the maṇḍala realm.
One should know that the syllable *jī* belongs to the Buddha family, the syllable *jra* to the Vajra family,
the syllable *jrā* to the Lotus family, and the syllable *a-kṣa* to the Karma family;
these are the root syllables of these families, which are constantly employed within the maṇḍala.
"This is called the Great Vajra Maṇḍala of All Tathāgatas.

At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, further expounded the various dharma-gates of accomplishment (*siddhi*), near-accomplishment (*upasiddhi*), great accomplishment (*mahāsiddhi*), and so forth:
"If one wishes to practice accomplishment, one should engage in the secret conduct of food and drink as appropriate."
That mind abides in the great luminous mind; this is the method of the corresponding samādhi.
If one desires to attain proximate accomplishment, one should practice according to the rite for one month.
All Buddhas skillfully bestow all accomplishments; this is what the Wisdom Vajra has taught.
If one desires to attain the great illumination and the great accomplishment, one should practice for three months;
this initial application of the conduct of equanimity was taught by Vajrapāṇi himself.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, further expounded the Dharma-gate of the Jewel-Treasury Samādhi for the accomplishment of the Wisdom Family and others:
"The practitioner should contemplate their own body as being none other than Vairocana Buddha.
By means of the vajra-wheel employed by one's own family, one attains the accomplishment of a Vidyādhara of the Vajra-Wheel."
The practitioner should contemplate their own body as being Vairocana Buddha;
through the great mantra of his own family, the vajra-sword, they shall achieve the vidyādhara state by holding the vajra-sword.
The practitioner should contemplate their own body as being Vairocana Buddha.
The trident is the great vidyā of the family of flowers; by attaining the samādhi of the trident, one achieves accomplishment.
The practitioner should contemplate their own body as being Vairocana Buddha;
the family vidyā is the vajra-hook, and by attaining that, one achieves the accomplishment of the vajra-hook.
The practitioner should contemplate his own body as being Vairocana Buddha;
through the great vidyā-mantra of his own family, the Vajra-noose, he attains the accomplishment of a Vidyādhara of the Vajra-noose.
Furthermore, one should contemplate that [the deity] arises from one's own reflected image, with the various marks such as the secret mahāmudrā;
thus holding that wish-fulfilling jewel, one thoroughly discerns the dharmas of all families.
If one wishes to accomplish this dharma of samādhi, one should accomplish the matters of accomplishment;
such a person will attain accomplishment in the present life through the sovereign dharma corresponding to the great vidyā-mantra.
If one does not accomplish the dharma of samādhi, that person shall be unable to behold the Buddha.
If one practices according to the fourfold ritual procedure, And dwells in reality through the union of visualization and contemplation,
One should know that what arises from one's own body Is the appearance corresponding to the reflection of one's own mind.
Having visualized clearly within the reflected image, one will swiftly achieve accomplishment without distinction;
as the utpala lotus is exceedingly pure, so too is the great mantra of its own family.
Contemplating according to the rite within the reflection of the moon, the vidyādhara of great wisdom attains accomplishment;
further visualizing the emergence of the mind-vajra, the vidyādhara of great wisdom attains accomplishment.
Within the light of that moon-image, one should contemplate Vajrapāṇi with a focused mind;
one should know that all desires are pure as the self, just as that space is pure, so too is it.
Within the light of that moon-image, one should visualize the appearance of the vajra-lotus.
Next, one should visualize the pure lotus-eye, which attains mastery over all stages;
within the light of that lunar reflection, one should imagine the appearance of the five Tathāgatas,
whose fivefold radiance is most subtle and wondrous, manifesting extensively and pervasively throughout the Buddha-body.
From within the light, the radiance of the sun further emerges; visualize the *karmavajra* appearing from the heart.
Recite the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) of your own family with a sincere mind, and you will immediately attain the firm adamantine body (*vajrakāya*).
Within the light of that lunar reflection, visualize the vajra of your own family.
Visualize the five-pronged vajra, and you shall immediately attain the indestructible vajra body;
within the light of that lunar reflection, manifest the appearance adorned with vajra flames.
Vajrapāṇi is himself this very image; visualize him holding the most sublime form.
Within the light of that moon-image, visualize the appearance of lotus-flame adornments;
Avalokiteśvara himself, as his own image, holds the magnificent color-form of the Great Dharma.
Within the light of that moon-image, visualize the appearance of white-flame adornments.
Kāmayam is one's own reflected image; visualize and maintain the form and characteristics of Kāmayam.
This single-syllable vidyā-mantra is the gateway to the seed of wisdom; it manifests as the form of the Great Powerful Vidyārāja.
One should visualize all the mudrās of the presiding deity of one’s own family, as well as one’s own mudrā.
Regarding the various great mudrās of body, speech, and mind, one should visualize each according to the appropriate ritual method.
Abiding within the samādhi of reality, one should clearly visualize the form of Vajrapāṇi;
within the light of that solar image, one should meditate upon one’s own mudrā as it truly is.
Furthermore, within the solar maṇḍala, one should clearly visualize one’s own form;
placing the syllables of the great mantra upon the heart, one should abide free from doubt and fear according to the ritual procedure.
Furthermore, one should visualize the arising of Vajrasattva, who is able to give birth to meditative concentration and the dharmas that emerge from it;
by relying on the fundamental ritual for the near-attainment of the practice, one immediately obtains all supreme accomplishments.
In accordance with the Dharma and as appropriate for the location, perform the rites of offering during the six months;
following the ritual of Vajrasattva, one will immediately attain supreme accomplishment in the three realms.
Wherever the practitioner performs the rite of accomplishment, empowered by Vajrasattva,
all those desired to be summoned— from devas and humans down to the bhūtas— will gather together.
The practitioner should select a secluded place, whether in a wilderness or among the mountains;
once all those who are to be summoned have arrived, one should perform the secret offerings according to the ritual.
Relying on that method of Vajrasattva, when performing the rite of summoning,
one should recite the mantra used for one's own family and form the great mudrā of that family.
Having bound the mudrā of the primary maṇḍala according to the ritual, one should recite with single-minded devotion to seek union;
at the hour of midnight, whatever the practitioner performs shall be accomplished accordingly.

Visualize a vajra hook placed at the heart; performing the yoga according to the rite of one's own family, the great light of the kalpa-fire blazes intensely, and the vajra hook appears within that light.
Visualize a vajra hook at the heart; according to the rite,
summon with a focused mind the wrathful king Yamāntaka, as well as Hayagrīva and the other vidyārājas,
all the Vajradanda vidyārājas, and the wrathful deity Acala.
His majestic radiance manifests extensively throughout the three realms; With a frowning brow, he gazes about.
The Great Powerful Wrathful Mahāvidyārāja, Together with that Amṛtakuṇḍalī, Arouses feelings of reverence and affection within the three realms; He is valiant and possesses great sovereign power.
That Lord of Great Mantras of Vajra Incense, whose power is equal to that of Vajrapāṇi,
constantly recites the name of the Buddha Tathāgata and abides in the indestructibility of the three vajras;
together with the Great Messenger of the Vajra Nācī and the Honored One Vajracaṇḍa.
Relying entirely upon the method of Vajrasattva, may all beings throughout the three realms be pervaded by *āveśa*;
even if the various poisons should fill the entirety of space, they can all be destroyed in a single kṣaṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again entered the samādhi of the Vajra of All Samādhis.
Emerging from this samādhi, he proclaimed the great vidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Yamāntaka, saying: "Namo vajrajñānāya. (1)
Samaya-sattvāya oṃ kara kara kuru kuru.
Mamakaḷyaṃ pañca vajra vajra sarvavighnān daha daha.

"The Secret, Pure Mahāyāna Dharma, The treasury of merit, the supreme wisdom within wisdom,
The universal gateway of great wisdom and selflessness— I take refuge in and praise this secret wisdom!"
The secret, true, and pure meaning, the supreme dharma like a great ocean,
born from the body of Samantabhadra— I take refuge in and praise the Vajra Wisdom;
the most excellent Great Wisdom, as it is mounted, abides unbreakably in the three vajras.
To the great Dharma-gate that has reached the further shore, I pay homage and praise the conduct of Bodhi;
To the supreme birth of all sentient beings, who cause all to enter the wisdom of the Buddhas;
To the unsurpassed self-nature purity of all Buddhas, I pay homage and praise the Savior of Beings.
The pure dharmakāya of great liberation, Like a wish-fulfilling gem of great sovereignty,
The gateway to liberation for all sentient beings— I take refuge in and praise your pure conduct.
At that time, there was in the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnasaṃdhivajra, who came forward and addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāguhyakādhipati Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"O Great Being!
"If there are bodhisattvas who wish to seek such dharmas of great merit, how should they seek them?
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, addressed the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇisamaya-vajra, saying: "Good son!
If there is a bodhisattva who gives rise to the thought of being free from doubt, they should seek in this way:
one who gives rise to the thought of being free from doubt should seek the Buddha-dharma;
one who gives rise to the thought of being free from doubt should seek all dharmas.
Regarding the arising of the thought that dispels doubt: one should contemplate all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) as they truly are.
Son of good family!

For example, a Bodhisattva dwelling on the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*) remains far removed from all conceptualization and all doubt regarding the *dharmakāya* of all Tathāgatas, the *saṃbhogakāya* of all Tathāgatas, and the *nirmāṇakāya* of all Tathāgatas; he dwells within all phenomena with the vision of reality (*yathābhūta-darśana*). It is likewise for one who knows these secret dharmas of great merit as they truly are.
"In short, this secret dharma is itself the great vajra wisdom of the bodhisattvas.

When all the Tathāgatas heard these words, they marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence. Immediately, a great mark of a mahāpuruṣa appeared, and within the assembly, they prostrated at the feet of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, and spoke thus:
"O Mahāsattva!..."

Regarding this dharma-gate of the practices of the secret great vidyā-mantras of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), what is the meaning of the fact that within these teachings there are those who develop faith and those who do not?
Vajrapāṇi said:
“For example, if all sentient beings in a trichiliocosm, as numerous as motes of dust, were all able to realize unsurpassed bodhi—would such a thing be believable?”
Is it not to be trusted?
O Mahāsattva!
This secret dharma-gate should also be viewed in this way; to view it in this way is to be free from conceptualized views.
At that time, the great beings emanated by all the Tathāgatas were filled with great joy and, marveling at such an unprecedented occurrence, spoke these verses:
“Great indeed is wisdom, O Great Wisdom! The Great Vajra has appeared, And the blind of the world Have obtained the purity of the eye of wisdom.”

At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, again entered the vajra-samādhi of the non-dual equality of all vajras. From within this samādhi, there issued forth hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of light rays, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, illuminating unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields in the southeastern direction, as many as the atoms contained therein.

All the great bodhisattvas within these buddha-fields who were illuminated by this light attained the perfect wisdom of the three bodies (*trikāya*). All Tathāgatas came to abide in the bodhicitta, and all sentient beings entered the fearless practice-gate of the self-nature of bodhi. They dwelt securely in the supreme vajra self-nature of the great wisdom-dharma-gate, which is like space, equal, adamantine, characterized by the signlessness of all phenomena, free from conceptual proliferation, and unborn.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, arose serenely from samādhi and addressed the great assembly, saying:
"O Noble Ones!
"One should give rise to the view of equality toward all sentient beings, conceiving of them as the Buddhas.

At that time, the emanated Great Being withdrew back into the treasury of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas and suddenly vanished. Those Tathāgatas and great Bodhisattvas who had come from the ten directions each dwelt, in accordance with reality, within the secret corresponding dharma of their own respective minds. Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, likewise dwelt within the true dharma of the secret correspondence of his own body, speech, and mind.
